message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live data feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact Air Quality Index (AQI) for Los Angeles at this moment. However, you can quickly check the current conditions using one of the following reliable sources:

| Source | How to Use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit [airnow.gov](https://www.airnow.gov/) and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. It shows the AQI, pollutant levels, and health advisories. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to [aqicn.org](https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/) for a live map, hourly updates, and historical data. |
| **Weather Apps** | Many weather apps (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or the built‑in weather app on iOS/Android) display AQI for major cities. |
| **Local News** | Local TV stations often report on air quality during severe pollution events. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities or have respiratory concerns, it’s a good idea to check the AQI before heading out. If you’d like, I can explain how to interpret the AQI values and what each range means for health.
